title: Transformation Geometry: Coordinates, Rules and Enlargements
seo_title: Grade 9 Transformation Geometry Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise, describe and perform transformations with points, line segments and simple geometric figures on a coordinate plane, including reflection in the line y = x; identify what the transformation of a point is if given the coordinates of its image; use proportion to describe the effect of enlargement or reduction on area and perimeter of geometric figures.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 9 transformation worksheets: translations, reflections, rotations and enlargements with coordinate rules. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Enlarge by k: lengths × k, area × k².
key_sub: Reflect in y = x: swap x and y.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Translation: (x; y) → (x + a; y + b).
  • Reflection in the y-axis: (x; y) → (−x; y); in y = x: (x; y) → (y; x).
  • Rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin: (x; y) → (y; −x).
  • Enlargement by k: (x; y) → (kx; ky). Lengths × k, area × k².

Examples

Example

Enlarge a 3 cm² shape by scale factor 2

area × 2²

Answer: 12 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong axisReflect in the y-axis: change x.
The wrong wayCheck clockwise or anti-clockwise.
Area × kArea changes by k².

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 9 say about transformations?
faq.a: Recognise, describe and perform transformations with points, line segments and figures on a coordinate plane, and investigate the effect of enlargement on area and perimeter.

faq.q: What happens to the perimeter in an enlargement by 3?
What is the image of (2; 5) reflected in y = x?
Is a reflection a rigid transformation?
faq.a: Yes, it keeps the size and shape.

items.e:

items.e:

−2. Where is its image?
items.e: The top number moves right 4; the bottom number moves down 2. Image: (3, 2).

items.e:
Top: across (−2), bottom: up/down (−5): −2

items.q:
The point (0, −4) is translated by the vector −3
1. Where is its image?
items.e: The top number moves left 3; the bottom number moves up 1. Image: (−3, −3).

items.q:
The point (−2, −5) is translated by the vector 5
3. Where is its image?
items.e: The top number moves right 5; the bottom number moves up 3. Image: (3, −2).

items.q: Translate (4, −3) 7 units left. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 7 units left: x: 4 − 7 = −3, y stays −3. (4, −3) → (−3, −3).

items.q: Translate (−2, 5) 6 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 6 units down: x stays −2, y: 5 − 6 = −1. (−2, 5) → (−2, −1).

items.q: Translate (−6, −1) 9 units right. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 9 units right: x: −6 + 9 = 3, y stays −1. (−6, −1) → (3, −1).

items.q: Translate (−4, 3) 6 units right and 5 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 6 units right and 5 units down: x: −4 + 6 = 2, y: 3 − 5 = −2. (−4, 3) → (2, −2).

items.q: Translate (5, −2) 7 units left and 4 units up. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 7 units left and 4 units up: x: 5 − 7 = −2, y: −2 + 4 = 2. (5, −2) → (−2, 2).

items.q: Translate (−1, −6) 5 units right and 8 units up. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 5 units right and 8 units up: x: −1 + 5 = 4, y: −6 + 8 = 2. (−1, −6) → (4, 2).

items.q: Translate (6, 2) 4 units left and 6 units down. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Translate 4 units left and 6 units down: x: 6 − 4 = 2, y: 2 − 6 = −4. (6, 2) → (2, −4).

items.q: Point P is translated 5 units right and 4 units down. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (−4, 1). Translate 5 units right and 4 units down: x: −4 + 5 = 1, y: 1 − 4 = −3. (−4, 1) → (1, −3). That is point B. Point C moves the wrong way up or down, point A swaps the two amounts, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 7 units left and 3 units up. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (5, −2). Translate 7 units left and 3 units up: x: 5 − 7 = −2, y: −2 + 3 = 1. (5, −2) → (−2, 1). That is point A. Point C moves the wrong way up or down, point B swaps the two amounts, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 units left and 2 units down. Which point is its image?
items.e: P is at (3, 4). Translate 5 units left and 2 units down: x: 3 − 5 = −2, y: 4 − 2 = 2. (3, 4) → (−2, 2). That is point C. Point B moves the wrong way up or down, point A swaps the two amounts, and point D comes from counting grid lines instead of spaces.

items.q: The point (−2, −4) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates. Image: (−4, −2).

items.q: The point (3, 0) is reflected in the line x = −2. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−7, 0).

items.q: The point (2, −4) is reflected in the line x = −1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−4, −4).

items.q: The point (−3, −2) is reflected in the line x = 1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (5, −2).

items.q: The point (2, 3) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates. Image: (3, 2).

items.q: The point (4, −2) is reflected in the line x = 2. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (0, −2).

items.q: The point (−3, 5) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates. Image: (5, −3).

items.q: The point (−2, −5) is reflected in the line y = 1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a horizontal line changes the y-coordinate only. Image: (−2, 7).

items.q: The point (−2, 1) is reflected in the line y = −x. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in y = −x swaps the coordinates and changes both signs. Image: (−1, 2).

items.q: The point (0, −3) is reflected in the line x = −1. What are the coordinates of its image?
items.e: Reflecting in a vertical line changes the x-coordinate only: the point is as far on the other side. Image: (−2, −3).

items.q: Reflect (4, −5) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (4, −5) → (−4, −5).

items.q: Reflect (−3, 6) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−3, 6) → (−3, −6).

items.q: Reflect (5, 2) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (5, 2) → (5, −2).

items.q: Reflect (−6, −3) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−6, −3) → (6, −3).

items.q: Reflect (−2, −4) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−2, −4) → (−2, 4).

items.q: Reflect (1, 6) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (1, 6) → (−1, 6).

items.q: Reflect (−6, 0) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−6, 0) is on the x-axis (the mirror line), so it stays at (−6, 0).

items.q: Reflect (0, 4) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (0, 4) is on the y-axis, 4 units above the x-axis. Reflect in the x-axis: y changes sign, 4 → −4. The image is 4 units below: (0, −4).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−4, 3). Reflect in the x-axis: x stays, y changes sign. (−4, 3) → (−4, −3). That is point C. Point A is the reflection in the y-axis instead, and point B changes both signs.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (5, −3). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (5, −3) → (−5, −3). That is point A. Point B is the reflection in the x-axis instead, and point C changes both signs.

items.q: The point (−1, 5) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−1, 5) from the centre becomes (−5, −1). Image: (−5, −1).

items.q: The point (5, 1) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Rotating 180° about the origin changes both signs. Image: (−5, −1).

items.q: The point (5, −1) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Rotating 180° about the origin changes both signs. Image: (−5, 1).

items.q: The point (−2, −2) is rotated 180° about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−1, −4) from the centre becomes (1, 4). Image: (0, 6).

items.q: The point (3, −4) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Rotating 180° about the origin changes both signs. Image: (−3, 4).

items.q: The point (−4, 1) is rotated 180° about the point (2, 0). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (−6, 1) from the centre becomes (6, −1). Image: (8, −1).

items.q: The point (4, −4) is rotated 180° about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (5, −6) from the centre becomes (−5, 6). Image: (−6, 8).

items.q: The point (4, 5) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (4, 5) from the centre becomes (−5, 4). Image: (−5, 4).

items.q: The point (2, 2) is rotated 90° clockwise about the point (−1, 2). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (3, 0) from the centre becomes (0, −3). Image: (−1, −1).

items.q: The point (2, −1) is rotated 180° about the point (1, 1). Where is its image?
items.e: Use tracing paper, or turn the position relative to the centre: (1, −2) from the centre becomes (−1, 2). Image: (0, 3).

items.q: Rotate (3, 5) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (3, 5) → (5, −3).

items.q: Rotate (−4, 2) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−4, 2) → (2, 4).

items.q: Rotate (−1, −6) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−1, −6) → (−6, 1).

items.q: Rotate (6, −3) 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (6, −3) → (3, 6).

items.q: Rotate (2, 4) 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (2, 4) → (−4, 2).

items.q: Rotate (−5, 3) 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (−5, 3) → (−3, −5).

items.q: Rotate (4, −6) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 180°: both signs change. (4, −6) → (−4, 6).

items.q: Rotate (−2, −3) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Rotate 180°: both signs change. (−2, −3) → (2, 3).

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (4, 2). Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (4, 2) → (2, −4). That is point A. Point B is a turn the wrong way, and point C only swaps the numbers.

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° anti-clockwise about the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (−3, 5). Rotate 90° anti-clockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the first one. (−3, 5) → (−5, −3). That is point C. Point A is a turn the wrong way, and point B only swaps the numbers.

items.q: A rectangle 7 cm by 3 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. What are the new side lengths?
c: 2 13 cm by 1 cm
items.e: Multiply every length by 3: 21 cm by 9 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: The point (0, −2) is enlarged by scale factor 3 with centre the origin. Where is its image?
items.e: From the origin, multiply both coordinates by 3: (0, −6).

items.q: A side of length 12 cm becomes 3 cm after an enlargement. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length = 3 ÷ 12 = 0,25.

items.q: A rectangle 5 cm by 4 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 2: 10 cm by 8 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A side of length 4 cm becomes 10 cm after an enlargement. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length = 10 ÷ 4 = 2,5.

items.q: A rectangle 5 cm by 7 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. What are the new side lengths?
c: 1 23 cm by 2 13 cm
items.e: Multiply every length by 3: 15 cm by 21 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 6 cm by 5 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 2: 12 cm by 10 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 2: 16 cm by 10 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 4 cm by 8 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. What are the new side lengths?
c: 1 13 cm by 2 23 cm
items.e: Multiply every length by 3: 12 cm by 24 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: A rectangle 5 cm by 6 cm is enlarged by scale factor 2. What are the new side lengths?
items.e: Multiply every length by 2: 10 cm by 12 cm. (A scale factor below 1 makes the shape smaller.)

items.q: Dilate (3, −2) by a scale factor of 2 with the centre at the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Dilate by 2: multiply both coordinates by 2. 3 × 2 = 6 and −2 × 2 = −4. (3, −2) → (6, −4).

items.q: Dilate (−4, 1) by a scale factor of 3 with the centre at the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Dilate by 3: multiply both coordinates by 3. −4 × 3 = −12 and 1 × 3 = 3. (−4, 1) → (−12, 3).

items.q: Dilate (−2, −5) by a scale factor of 2 with the centre at the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Dilate by 2: multiply both coordinates by 2. −2 × 2 = −4 and −5 × 2 = −10. (−2, −5) → (−4, −10).

items.q: Dilate (8, −6) by a scale factor of 12 with the centre at the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Dilate by 12: multiply both coordinates by 12, which halves them. 8 ÷ 2 = 4 and −6 ÷ 2 = −3. (8, −6) → (4, −3).

items.q: Dilate (−6, 4) by a scale factor of 12 with the centre at the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Dilate by 12: multiply both coordinates by 12, which halves them. −6 ÷ 2 = −3 and 4 ÷ 2 = 2. (−6, 4) → (−3, 2).

items.q: Dilate (1, −2) by a scale factor of 3 with the centre at the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: Dilate by 3: multiply both coordinates by 3. 1 × 3 = 3 and −2 × 3 = −6. (1, −2) → (3, −6).

items.q: Point P is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with the centre at the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (2, −3). Dilate by 2: multiply both coordinates by 2. 2 × 2 = 4 and −3 × 2 = −6. (2, −3) → (4, −6). That is point C. Point A comes from adding 2 instead of multiplying, and points B and D multiply only one coordinate.

items.q: Point P is dilated by a scale factor of 3 with the centre at the origin. Which point is the image?
items.e: P is at (−2, 1). Dilate by 3: multiply both coordinates by 3. −2 × 3 = −6 and 1 × 3 = 3. (−2, 1) → (−6, 3). That is point A. Point B comes from adding 3 instead of multiplying, and points C and D multiply only one coordinate.

items.q: Triangle B is a dilation of triangle A with the centre at the origin. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Compare a vertex and its image: (3, 1) → (6, 2). Each coordinate is multiplied by 2. Check a side: the bottom side of A is 2 units long and the bottom side of B is 4 units long. B is bigger, so the scale factor is more than 1. (12 would take B back to A.)

items.q: Triangle B is a dilation of triangle A with the centre at the origin. What is the scale factor?
items.e: Compare a vertex and its image: (6, 4) → (3, 2). Each coordinate is multiplied by 12. Check a side: the bottom side of A is 4 units long and the bottom side of B is 2 units long. B is smaller, so the scale factor is less than 1. (2 would take B back to A.)

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 3), B(3, 3), C(1, 6). It is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of B′?
items.e: B(3, 3) is reflected in the y-axis, so B′ is (−3, 3).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 1), B(5, 1), C(3, 4). It is translated 4 units left and 5 units down. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(3, 4) is translated 4 units left and 5 units down, so C′ is (−1, −1).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 3), B(4, 3), C(2, 5). It is translated 5 units left and 5 units down. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(2, 3) is translated 5 units left and 5 units down, so A′ is (−3, −2).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 2), B(4, 2), C(1, 5). It is translated 3 units right and 5 units down. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(1, 2) is translated 3 units right and 5 units down, so A′ is (4, −3).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 2), B(5, 2), C(2, 4). It is translated 4 units left and 3 units up. What are the coordinates of B′?
items.e: B(5, 2) is translated 4 units left and 3 units up, so B′ is (1, 5).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 1), B(6, 1), C(3, 3). It is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of B′?
items.e: B(6, 1) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin, so B′ is (1, −6).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 2), B(5, 2), C(2, 5). It is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(2, 5) is reflected in the x-axis, so C′ is (2, −5).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 3), B(4, 3), C(1, 5). It is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(1, 5) is reflected in the x-axis, so C′ is (1, −5).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 2), B(4, 2), C(2, 4). It is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of C′?
items.e: C(2, 4) is reflected in the x-axis, so C′ is (2, −4).

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, 1), B(5, 1), C(3, 4). It is rotated 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A(3, 1) is rotated 180° about the origin, so A′ is (−3, −1).

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Triangle B is the same size and points the same way as triangle A: it only slid. That is a translation (6 units right and 6 units down).

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (−2, 1) → (2, 1). Reflect in the y-axis: y stays, x changes sign. (−2, 1) → (2, 1). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a reflection in the y-axis.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Follow one vertex: (5, 1) → (−5, −1). Rotate 180°: both signs change. (5, 1) → (−5, −1). Check the other vertices: they all land on triangle B, so it is a rotation of 180°.

items.q: Which single transformation maps triangle A onto triangle B?
items.e: Triangle B has the same shape as triangle A but is bigger, so it is a dilation. Dilate by 3: multiply both coordinates by 3. 2 × 3 = 6 and 1 × 3 = 3. (2, 1) → (6, 3). Translations, reflections and rotations never change the size.

items.q: Triangle PQR has vertices (−1, 3), (−1, 5), (−4, 5). Its image has vertices (3, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), in the same order. Which single transformation was used?
items.e: Compare each vertex with its image. Rotate 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). Swap the numbers, then change the sign of the second one. (−1, 3) → (3, 1). The rule works for every vertex, so it is a rotation of 90° clockwise.

items.q: Triangle PQR has vertices (1, 2), (2, 2), (2, 1). Its image has vertices (3, 6), (6, 6), (6, 3), in the same order. Which single transformation was used?
items.e: Compare each vertex with its image. Dilate by 3: multiply both coordinates by 3. 1 × 3 = 3 and 2 × 3 = 6. (1, 2) → (3, 6). The rule works for every vertex, so it is a dilation. The image is similar to the triangle, with sides 3 times as long.

items.q: Which transformation can change the size of a shape?
items.e: Translations, reflections and rotations give a congruent image (same size and shape). A dilation gives a similar image that can be larger or smaller.

items.q: On a grid map of a canoe trip in Algonquin Park, the campsite is at (−5, −2). A canoe paddles 7 units right and 5 units up. Where does it land?
items.e: Translate 7 units right and 5 units up: x: −5 + 7 = 2, y: −2 + 5 = 3. (−5, −2) → (2, 3).

items.q: Kagiso draws a loon on a calm lake. The shoreline is the x-axis, and the tip of the loon’s beak is at (3, 4). He draws the loon’s reflection in the water. Where is the tip of the reflected beak?
items.e: The water line is the x-axis, so reflect in the x-axis: x stays 3, y changes sign. (3, 4) → (3, −4).

items.q: A drawing of a canoe is 8 cm long. The class dilates it by a scale factor of 12 to fit on a bookmark. How long is the canoe on the bookmark?
items.e: Multiply by 12: 8 × 12 = 4 cm. (16 cm is multiplying by 2, and 7,5 cm is subtracting 12.)
